questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good university reputation and my friend went to Edinburgh and said that the city had many vegan options.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The semester started with Covid restrictions so it was hard to socialize in the beginning.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was difficult because I lived far from campus and I had to navigate multiple mailboxes.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a guidance councillor to speak to. Apart from that I had to figure everything on my own.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I never received orientation and I missed the online sessions because of a private matter.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficult. I applied for housing months beforehand but received no word. I called a month before my departure and they told me that there was not a space for me. I had to find my own after that and there was only 1 accommodation available north from the city.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: A Ridacard makes exploring the city fantastic (and gets you into uni cheap).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I wish they would have told me that they did not have a space earlier.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The host institution was much clearer than my home university.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Because I am from the EU I could do it online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could send mails to the help desk.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Somewhat.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find your guidance councillor first. They know everything.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Although I did not receive the course I really wanted, the ones I got were very thorough and well structured.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took my electives on exchange, which were at a lower level. They were connected to my major so the courses ended up not being difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In some classes they encourage you to read first and then attend class and in others it is the opposite. People speak less during class (I spoke a lot). It is difficult to say overall because the Zoom format is pretty much the same. There are tutorials, which are alike UCPH's seminars. They allow for less formal discussion.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
History of Art 1B
History of Art 2B
Objects of Desire

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The History of Art courses were excellent from the structure to the teaching!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The inflation.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Fresh produce was much much cheaper than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The semester started off with Covid so there were not many opportunities. After a while they came and they were alright.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Societies and the parties they organized.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Book Club (you don't have to read the book and they do pub nights etc.) and a class near your subject (ex. History of Art Society).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: To go on a trip up to the highlands!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: As well as being Danish I am from another English speaking country and found the culture very familiar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join societies!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of focus on Instagram numbers, which can be very superficial.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Ceilidhs, and how friendly and talkative people were.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Cheap food (vegan) 
2. Download Whatsapp 
3. Great bus service (okay to live outside the city)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to the museums (they're free!)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: New friends and reading techniques.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Loneliness from Covid, not a lot of social event organized by the host institution, and that there were more people in the autumn semester than the spring semester at my accommodation.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Edinburgh has a fantastic food scene.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
